source.title: The Implicit Bias of Logit Regularization
source.authors: A. Beck; Yohai Bar-Sinai; N. Levi

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or wrong-document problem; the supplied text includes the paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Reports delayed generalization in a different, non-algorithmic linear-classification setting and directly contrasts logit regularization with weight decay, finding that weight decay does not produce the same interpolation-threshold shift.
record.gate_note: The paper reports grokking-like dynamics for its own synthetic signal-plus-noise classification experiments. Its CIFAR-10 feature results measure final accuracy, not delayed generalization. References to grokking results from other papers are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study's own experiments report delayed generalization with non-monotonic test loss in a new setting. That setting is linear classifiers trained by full-batch gradient descent on synthetic Gaussian signal-plus-noise data. The delay is switched on by weak convex logit regularization (absent at alpha=0) and diverges as alpha approaches 0. This is a result on V3's 'non-algorithmic data, set by the training regime' part. The paper does not argue that any version is wrong, so T3 fits better than T5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that convex logit regularization induces logit clustering around finite targets and aligns weights with Fisher's discriminant for Gaussian data or quadratic loss. It shifts the noiseless interpolation threshold to lambda=1, induces grokking under weak regularization in 1/2<lambda<1, and makes accuracy invariant to orthogonal noise. Weight decay lacks the threshold shift and the noise invariance.
record.recipe_differences: Uses linear classifiers on synthetic signal-plus-noise data and a logit penalty, rather than small algorithmic datasets and the original grokking setup. The paper also evaluates frozen ResNet-18 features, but does not report grokking dynamics for that evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported grokking delay depends on logit regularization strength alpha and diverges as alpha approaches zero. The weight-decay comparison reports dependence on orthogonal noise scale.

fits_no_version.finding: In a linear model, L2 weight decay does not shift the noiseless interpolation threshold: accuracy is not 100% for 0.5<lambda<1, and it stays sensitive to sigma_n. Convex logit regularization instead gives perfect generalization if and only if d/N<1 (Prop. 5.1, Fig. 16).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Per-sample logit penalties, unlike weight-norm penalties, set a critical sample size (N>d) beyond which a regularized linear model generalizes perfectly.

record.problems: The grokking evidence is from synthetic linear-classification settings, with no reported uncertainty estimates. The dynamics are shown in figures without numerical accuracy values. The realistic-feature experiment reports final accuracy rather than delayed generalization.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant delayed-generalization rows were extracted from the CIFAR-10/ResNet-18 feature experiments (Figures 3 and 9), which report feature geometry and final accuracy rather than training-time grokking. Other geometry, clustering, and accuracy results do not measure the delayed-generalization behavior or low-norm efficiency account.

untested.parts: No algorithmic datasets. The delay is varied through alpha, not training-set size, and Fig. 5 uses only lambda=0.7.
No circuit or mechanistic progress measures. Logit snapshots are shown, but no continuous measure is tested as anticipating the jump.

No real images, text or molecules with grokking dynamics: the ResNet-18/CIFAR features (Fig. 9) report only final accuracy. Initialization scale, weight norm and a lazy-to-rich transition are not varied. The switch tested is logit regularization strength.
No efficient-circuit comparison, no critical dataset size under weight decay, and no ungrokking. The weight-decay runs report only final accuracy.
Algorithms are not compared across runs or architectures.
Optimizer and numerical-precision causes of the delay are not tested.

missing.what: Threshold shift with logit regularization: perfect generalization only for lambda=d/N<1 versus 1/2 unregularized. This is a critical-sample-size result relevant to comparing with V5-style critical dataset size, though it comes from logit regularization rather than weight decay.
At larger alpha (0.2, Fig. 4), generalization reaches 100% without a pronounced delay. This confirms the delay appears only under weak regularization.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V5 'challenges' label is removed. The weight-decay runs report only final accuracy and do not test V5's efficiency account or ungrokking. The grokking evidence is figure-only, with no numbers or uncertainty. The paper cites prior unregularized grokking near lambda=1/2 (Beck et al. 2025); that is not a result of this study.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train on small algorithmic datasets or report the claimed training-set-size-dependent delay.
Does not identify a Fourier or other generalizing circuit, measure gradual circuit formation, or track removal of memorizing components.
Tests synthetic linear-classification settings, not grokking on realistic image, text, or molecule training. Does not vary initialization scale or weight norm or test a lazy-to-rich transition.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data.

Compares weight decay with logit regularization on generalization and the interpolation threshold, but does not test an efficient-circuit mechanism, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below that size.
Does not compare the algorithms learned across runs.
Does not test whether optimizer or numerical choices cause the delay or whether controlling them removes it.

relationships.condition: Linear classifiers on synthetic Gaussian signal-plus-noise data (sigma_f=0, lambda=0.7), binary and 10-class, with weak quadratic logit regularization.
relationships.reason: The delay appears on non-algorithmic data and is set by a regime choice: absent at alpha=0 (r1), present for alpha of 0.001 to 0.1 (r2-r4) and in the multi-class run (r5), diverging as alpha approaches 0. The data are synthetic Gaussian, not real images, text or molecules.
relationships.display_finding: Delays were absent at α=0, present for α=0.001–0.1 and in multiclass classification, and diverged as positive α approached zero.
